human_tolerance.notes: Skulking bird of thick shrubby vegetation in damp areas near ponds, lakes, marshes and rivers (Wikipedia).

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Authored window. Wikipedia: egg laying mid-to-late June in Europe, two broods a year, first breeding at one year old.

vocalizations.description: Loud, explosive burst of song from a low perch, given by males; the program sings at dawn and dusk. Season limits are not set by the sources read.
Short alarm call given when disturbed; the programme uses it as the flee trigger. Sound is authored, not from a recording.

range.note: Country list derived from 'breeds in southern and western Europe, northwest Africa and the east Palearctic as far as Afghanistan and northwest Pakistan' plus the Turkey-to-Iran orientalis subspecies line. Not checked against a distribution dataset. GB is excluded: first breeding 1972-73 after natural colonisation, status not assessed here.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Wikipedia describes a skulking habit; hop and fly inferred from passerine morphology, not stated in the source.

traits.flight.note: Short rounded wings; powered but weak flight, judged from the description.

traits.nest_type.note: Untidy cup-shaped nest in thick dense vegetation.

traits.perching.note: Passerine; perches on shrub twigs; not separately stated.

traits.mass_kg.note: Scholer mass column for row X=628 is 13.22 (units taken as grams; the dataset header does not state units). Wikipedia gives 15 g male and 12 g female, which bracket this value.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Sex-specific adult masses 12 g (female) and 15 g (male) from Wikipedia taken as the range.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Typical lifespan proxy: L = -1/ln(S) with S = 0.547 (annual adult survival, row X=628, mark-recapture, Mondego Valley, Portugal, se 0.111) = 1.66 years, rounded to 1.7. Assumes constant annual survival and adult-only input. The estimate is apparent survival, so it probably biases low if emigration occurs; juvenile mortality is excluded and would lower a whole-life mean. Not a maximum or captive age. Single population, so it may not represent other parts of the range.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia: 'insectivorous, preying on arthropods'; diet set to 1.0 invertebrate.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: males hold territories and sometimes attract more than one female; group size is judged.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Authored judgement: active by day; the species sings at dawn and dusk. Not from a sourced activity pattern.

traits.defense.note: Authored judgement: skulking, flees into cover.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: skulking shrub bird, moderate wariness.

habitat.note: Habitat from Wikipedia: thick shrubby vegetation in damp areas near water. Ground/arboreal split is an authored judgement.

seasonal.note: Breeding window authored from Wikipedia (June laying, two broods). Not a sourced date range; the nesting months are limited by the shared program.

vocalizations.note: Wikipedia: loud song in distinct bursts. Call descriptions and cooldowns are authored, not from recordings.

look.note: Plumage from Wikipedia (rich chestnut upperparts, pale grey-brown throat and breast, pale grey supercilium); colours and proportions are authored.

behavior.note: Shared program bt-perching-songbird-v1; limitations recorded in the PR.
